body:
Hi maintainers,

I’m interested in working on the Dart port mentioned in the Monero Bounties post:

https://bounties.monero.social/posts/166/1-000m-port-the-haveno-api-library-from-typescript-to-dart

Before starting implementation, I’d like to confirm the expected scope and acceptance criteria publicly.

Proposed scope:
- Create a Dart package equivalent to the core `haveno-ts` client API.
- Generate or maintain Dart gRPC/protobuf bindings for the Haveno daemon API.
- Implement a typed client with the main flows used in the current `haveno-ts` README sample:
  - connect to daemon
  - get balances
  - get payment accounts
  - get offers / my offers
  - take offer
  - disconnect
- Add focused tests for generated bindings/client wrappers and mockable gRPC behavior.
- Add README usage examples and setup instructions.

Questions:
1. Is this scope enough for the bounty, or is a full feature-for-feature port expected?
2. Should the Dart package live in a new repository, a fork, or under the Haveno organization?
3. Which maintainer should review/ACK the work?
4. Are there any existing contributors already working on this?
5. What exact criteria should be met for payout eligibility?

I won’t start implementation until there is public concept ACK from the project/maintainers so the work is aligned with Haveno’s expectations.
title: Clarify scope and acceptance criteria for Dart port bounty

body:
Here's a complete English bounty post template you can copy, paste, and adapt. It's designed to be easily parsed by bots (e.g., GitHub Actions, Discord "action board" scrapers) and follows typical Lean/Mathlib collaboration style.

```markdown
[Bounty] $XXX – Formalize (or disprove) the "Prime Emergence Conjecture"

## Problem in plain language
I propose a new conjecture related to prime emergence.  
*(Replace the following with your actual conjecture – keep it concise and precise)*

**Conjecture (natural language):**  
For every integer n > 1, there exists a prime p such that [your precise statement here].

## Formal statement (Lean 4 / Mathlib)
If you already have a Lean formalisation, put it below. Otherwise, a bounty hunter must produce one.

```lean
import Mathlib.Data.Nat.Prime
-- Example placeholder – replace with your own
example (n : ℕ) (hn : n > 1) : ∃ p, Prime p ∧ [your predicate] := sorry
```

Bounty goals

Choose one or both:

· A) Formalise the conjecture in Lean + prove it (requires a full proof that compiles with Mathlib).
  Bounty: $___ (paid via GitHub Sponsors / PayPal / crypto)
· B) Disprove the conjecture (provide a counterexample, either in natural language or formalised).
  Bounty: $___

Merge / acceptance criteria

For the bounty to be paid and the contribution merged:

· The work is submitted as a Pull Request to a public GitHub repository (e.g., my own repo or a designated “conjecture-collection” repo).
· The PR includes a clear lean file containing either a proof (with #check) or a concrete counterexample.
· All Lean code passes lean --verify and uses Mathlib 4 (latest stable).
· The PR is merged by me or a designated maintainer.

Optional – to make it "action board" friendly:

· Add label bounty / prime-emergence
· The PR description must contain the exact phrase "Prime Emergence Conjecture bounty"

License

All contributed code will be released under MIT (or CC0 / Apache 2.0). The mathematical statement itself is public domain.

How to claim

1. Fork [my-repo-link] / create a new PR in the target repository.
2. Write your proof/disproof.
3. Reference this bounty post in the PR description.
4. Once merged, I’ll pay the bounty within 7 days.

Contact / discussion

Open an issue in [my-repo-link] or ping me on [Discord/Keybase/Zulip].

```

### 🤖 Tips to make it machine‑scannable for an “action board”

Many bots watch for:

- **Keywords in title**: `[Bounty]`, `$`, `Prime Emergence Conjecture`
- **Checklist syntax**: `- [ ]` (GitHub task list)
- **Label**: add a label like `bounty` or `help-wanted`
- **Exact phrase**: put `"Prime Emergence Conjecture bounty"` in the PR body

If your “action board” is a specific Discord bot or GitHub Project automation, check its documentation – but the template above follows the common pattern used by **GitHub Issues**, **Gitcoin**, and **OnlyDust** bounties.

### ✏️ What you still need to fill in

- Your exact conjecture (replace the placeholder text)
- Bounty amount
- Your GitHub repo link (or specify where the PR should be sent)
- Your payment method

Once you have those, copy the template into a **GitHub Issue**, a **GitHub Gist**, or a **Discord channel** that the bot scans. Good luck!
```

References #33.

## Problem

The `Bounty task` issue template asks for a bounty amount as plain text:

```md
## Bounty Amount

$50
```

But the bounty program instructions in #33 require new bounty issues to include the machine-readable slash marker `/bounty $[amount]`. Issues created from the template can therefore omit the marker that contributors and automation use to identify reward-backed work.

## Expected behavior

The template should default to the same `/bounty $50` marker used by the seeded bounty issues and the program instructions.

## Acceptance criteria

- Update `.github/ISSUE_TEMPLATE/bounty_task.md` so the default bounty amount uses `/bounty $50`.
- Keep the change focused on the issue template and required AI agent metadata.
- Verify the template contains exactly one `/bounty $50` default marker.
title: Bounty issue template omits required /bounty marker

## Parent

https://github.com/KeygraphHQ/shannon/issues/360

## What to build

Register `bounty` as a top-level CLI subcommand and implement `bounty start` as a thin wrapper around the existing `spawnWorker` / `ensureInfra` machinery. Wire program config into the pipeline as scope rules and a new `bountyConfig` field on `PipelineInput`.

End-to-end path:
- `apps/cli/src/commands/bounty.ts` — dispatcher for `bounty start`; accepts `--url`, `--repo`, `--program <file|url>`, `--refresh-program`, `--workspace`, `--output`, `--debug`, `--pipeline-testing` (no `--config`)
- `bounty start` loads or parses `ProgramConfig` via the program config system (#364), then converts `in_scope_domains` → `rules.focus` URL patterns and `out_of_scope_patterns` → `rules.avoid` patterns, passed as `configData` overrides into `PipelineInput`
- New optional `bountyConfig?: BountyConfig` field added to `PipelineInput` and `shared.ts`; workflow passes it through to all activity inputs
- `apps/worker/prompts/shared/_bounty-mode.txt` — instructs agents to behave as a careful human researcher: space out requests, avoid brute-force patterns, vary timing, do not hammer auth endpoints; injected into all agent prompts when `bountyConfig` is present
- Active campaign info surfaced in the startup output (alongside Target / Repository / Workspace)

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] `./shannon bounty start -u <url> -r <repo> --program shopify.txt` runs a complete scan
- [ ] In-scope domains appear as `rules.focus` patterns visible in agent prompts
- [ ] Out-of-scope patterns appear as `rules.avoid` patterns visible in agent prompts
- [ ] `bountyConfig` present in `PipelineInput` and visible in Temporal workflow input
- [ ] `_bounty-mode.txt` partial appears in agent prompts during a bounty scan
- [ ] Active campaign name and multipliers printed at scan startup when present
- [ ] `./shannon bounty start --help` shows correct usage

## Blocked by

https://github.com/KeygraphHQ/shannon/issues/364

## What
When the player accumulates crimes, they become wanted. Bounty hunters pursue them. Faction patrols attack on sight.

**Bounty mechanics:** Crimes tracked per faction. When crimes exceed a threshold, player is wanted in that faction's territory. Bounty amount = crime severity × faction power. Bounty hunters have their own ship classes and AI — pursue the player across systems.

**Hiding reputation:** Player can pay off bounties at neutral stations (expensive). Letting time pass reduces notoriety but not crimes. Changing identity (new ship, false papers) is a major operation.

**Smuggling:** Blockade running without being caught. Scan evasion mechanics. Contraband detected during docking scans — bribes, smuggling compartments, or fast talk.

**Dependencies:** #35 (reputation), #29 (landed combat — bounty hunters on station)

- [ ] Bounty hunters pursue across systems
- [ ] Paying bounty removes wanted status

`.github/workflows/seed-meta-issue.yml` tells contributors to reference the canonical Bug Bounty Program issue in new bounty issues, but `.github/workflows/seed-issues.yml` creates starter bounty issues without any parent/canonical bounty reference.

That makes seeded issues less traceable than manually created bounty issues and breaks the workflow guidance that new bounty issues should point back to the program instructions.

## Expected

- Before creating starter issues, the workflow should find the existing non-PR issue titled `Bug Bounty Program — How to Participate`.
- Each seeded starter issue body should include a parent bounty reference such as `Parent bounty: #33` when that canonical issue is found.
- Keep the existing `/bounty $50` marker and seeded issue acceptance criteria unchanged.

## Scope

Keep the fix focused on `.github/workflows/seed-issues.yml` plus required AI agent metadata.

/bounty $50
title: Seeded starter bounty issues omit parent bounty reference

# Earn Bounties For Contributions

As a user, I want to earn bounties for contributing to protocol growth, so I'm
incentivized to take part in tasks.

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] A list of open bounties is visible in the UI with task description, reward
      amount, and acceptance criteria.
- [ ] A user can claim a bounty, submit proof of completion, and track the
      review status of their submission.
- [ ] Approved submissions trigger an on-chain payout to the contributor's
      wallet, with the transaction linked from the UI.
- [ ] Bounty funding draws from the configured fee allocation and the remaining
      bounty budget is visible to users.
